data.title: 'Not If, but When,' Says Top Investor About Microsoft Stock
data.description:
Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) stock has made an impressive recovery from its early summer lows and is now trading around $500, putting it fairly close to its previous record highs.

After facing negative sentiment regarding its AI positioning, the rebound reflects renewed confidence in the company's cloud and AI prospects. Azure growth has been a major part of that recovery, while Microsoft's broader software platform gives it multiple ways to benefit as businesses adopt AI agents and other advanced workloads.

The bigger question now is whether Microsoft is prepared to spend aggressively enough to meet future demand. According to investor JR Research, who ranks among the top 2% of investors on TipRanks, the answer appears to be yes. JR believes the company's latest signals point to a much more bullish view of long-term compute requirements than investors might have expected.

JR points to a recent Bloomberg report that suggests Microsoft could roughly triple its total compute capacity, from about 12 gigawatts today to as much as 38 GW by 2032. That figure includes both Microsoft-owned and leased facilities, so it should not be interpreted as a direct forecast for capital expenditure. Still, JR sees it as an important indication that Microsoft expects demand for computing power to remain strong for years.

The shift is notable because Microsoft had previously appeared more cautious about adding capacity, particularly amid concerns that the AI infrastructure boom could eventually create excess supply. JR believes that stance is changing as monetization opportunities become clearer and capacity constraints remain an issue.

Copilot is one reason for that confidence. Usage appears to be stabilizing, giving Microsoft a stronger foundation for expanding consumption and pricing over time. That makes a larger infrastructure commitment easier to justify because the company has more visibility into how the additional capacity can generate revenue.

Azure is also becoming harder for investors to overlook. Microsoft has disclosed that the cloud business has surpassed a $100 billion annualized revenue run rate, up from roughly $75 billion a year earlier. JR sees the decision to highlight Azure separately as a sign that Microsoft is ready to put its cloud growth opportunity more firmly in the spotlight.

There are still risks to the investment case, however. A much larger compute buildout could weigh on free cash flow margins and keep pressure on Microsoft's valuation until management provides more detail on the pace and economics of that spending. The company also remains heavily exposed to OpenAI, although its platform now supports around 11,000 models, giving it broader exposure across the AI ecosystem.

Even after the rally, JR believes the fundamental picture remains attractive. Microsoft trades at a little over 25 times forward earnings, below its roughly 30x average over the past five years. "The overall risk-reward remains favorable across its fundamentals, margins, visibility, and copilot adoption," the 5-star analyst summed up. "It positions the stock well in the next pullback for investors who are looking to double down before the re-rating advances further."

Accordingly, JR rates the stock a Buy. (To watch JR Research's track record, click here)

That is also the overwhelming opinion on Wall Street. The stock claims a Strong Buy consensus rating, based on 33 Buys vs. 1 Hold. Going by the $571.41 average price target, shares will be changing hands for a 14.5% premium a year from now. (See MSFT stock forecast)

data.title: SOUN Stock Drops 10% in a Month: Why Analysts See 90% Upside Ahead
data.description:
SoundHound AI (SOUN) stock has fallen 10% over the past month, extending its year-to-date decline to 36%. The stock is also down about 70% from its peak of more than $21 per share last October. Concerns about profitability and the stock's valuation continue to weigh on investor sentiment. Broader weakness across AI stocks has added to the pressure. Still, Wall Street remains bullish on SOUN, with a Strong Buy consensus rating and an average price target implying about 90% upside.

For context, SoundHound AI focuses on voice recognition and natural language processing, providing AI-powered solutions for multiple industries.

Why Investors Are Selling SOUN Stock

SoundHound's revenue growth remains strong. Q2 revenue jumped 45% year-over-year to $61.9 million. The company also raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $230 million-$260 million, from $225 million-$260 million.

However, profitability remains a concern. SoundHound has yet to turn a profit. In Q2, the company reported a $42.8 million GAAP net loss, while research and integration costs continued to weigh on its bottom line. For SOUN investors, the key question is whether the company can turn its rapid revenue growth into lasting profits.

Valuation is another problem. SoundHound's price-to-sales ratio stands at 13.37, well above the sector average of 3.60. This leaves less room for disappointment, as investors are already pricing in strong future growth.

Analysts Are Bullish on SOUN Stock

H.C. Wainwright analyst Scott Buck has a Street-high $20 price target, which implies more than 200% upside from recent levels. Buck expects SoundHound to reach adjusted EBITDA break-even by the end of 2026 while continuing to invest in growth. Although those investments could pressure near-term profits, he believes they can support long-term growth. Buck has also noted that SoundHound is expanding its partner base, which could help the company attract new customers and grow revenue.

Overall, Buck's bullish view is based on SoundHound's strong revenue growth and progress toward adjusted EBITDA break-even. The key risk is whether the company can turn that growth into sustained profits.

Meanwhile, Cantor Fitzgerald's analyst Thomas Blakey has a Buy rating with $15 price target, implying more than 135% upside. He said strong execution and rising demand for voice AI and AI agents could support further growth.

data.title: Pentagon Reports $33.4 Billion Iran War Bill While Fuel Price Spikes Cost American Households Over $800 Each
data.description:
The U.S. Department of War set the price tag for Operation Epic Fury, its fight against Iran, at $33.4 billion for the first four months. A top watchdog report shows that buying weapons makes up the biggest part of the bill at $22.3 billion. Operating costs added $7.4 billion, while broken or lost military gear added another $3.7 billion.

This big spending created real supply problems for American troops. Military buyers said using so many weapons so fast ran down safety stocks and slowed down deliveries. Congress has not passed a new funding law for the fight, so military units had to take funds out of basic budgets meant for normal training and routine upkeep. The White House asked for $87.6 billion in extra funds on June 24, with $21 billion set aside to buy replacement weapons.

The Financial Burden on American Families Has Grown

While the Pentagon reported a fixed $33.4 billion bill, the financial burden on American families has grown much higher. The official military report leaves out long-term repair costs and wider economic damage, such as the major oil price rise following trade friction near the Strait of Hormuz. A tracking study by Brown University shows that higher gas prices have drawn $106.5 billion out of American consumer budgets since February 28.

data.title: Oracle vs. Adobe: One AI Software Stock Is a Buy, the Other Is Too Problematic, Says Goldman Sachs
data.description:
Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) and Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) are two software giants trying to adapt to the new AI-driven paradigm, but both face huge challenges as they invest heavily in AI while trying to protect their existing businesses and justify their valuations. Oracle is betting big on AI infrastructure and cloud, while Adobe is working to defend its creative software franchise as generative AI reshapes how users create and consume content.

Both have also seen their share prices contract in 2026 as investors mull over the difficulties the two face, from the huge cost of building out AI infrastructure to the threat that AI could disrupt their core businesses.

So, are these software stalwarts doomed or do these stocks offer excellent value at their currently depressed states?

Promotion

Explore ORCZ for 2X short leverage on ORCL

Following the pair's recent earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges has been assessing their prospects and finds that only one is currently worth investors' attention.

For Oracle, Borges believes the latest quarter helped settle some of the concerns surrounding its huge AI infrastructure push. Revenue came in slightly ahead of expectations, while cloud infrastructure revenue jumped 121% year over year as new capacity came online. Oracle also delivered 850MW of capacity during the quarter and completed its planned $20 billion at-the-market share offering, removing an important funding concern.

The bigger questions, however, lie beyond the current fiscal year. Borges says investors still need a clearer picture of Oracle's capital spending requirements in fiscal 2028, how much additional funding the company will need and when it can return to positive free cash flow. For the stock to perform from here, she believes Oracle must continue adding capacity while proving that this investment is translating into backlog, revenue and ultimately gross profit. The analyst expects the company's October investor day to provide some much-needed detail on these issues.

All told, Borges expects Oracle to execute successfully. She maintained a Buy rating on the shares and raised the price target slightly from $239 to $240, implying the stock will gain 70% in the year ahead. (To watch Borges's track record, click here)

Adobe's results also offered some encouraging signs, particularly around user growth and engagement. Borges points to more than 1 billion monthly active users, with creative freemium users surpassing 100 million. Firefly's annual recurring revenue also grew 40% quarter-over-quarter, while AI-related ARR passed $650 million, up 150% YoY.

The challenge for Adobe is turning that engagement into sustainable revenue growth. The company has deliberately prioritized expanding its free user base and attracting new customers over near-term monetization, meaning investors now need to see how effectively those users convert into paying customers. Borges also notes that the shift toward more flexible, monthly subscriptions is weighing on RPO (remaining performance obligations). On top of that, the arrival of new CEO Anil Chakravarthy following David Wadhwani's departure adds another element of uncertainty as Adobe tries to balance AI innovation, user growth and monetization.

Put that altogether and the negatives outweigh the positives for Borges. She reiterated a Sell rating, backed by a $200 price target. That figure suggests the shares will slide by 23% over the coming months.

The Street also clearly distinguishes between the pair. Oracle claims a Strong Buy consensus rating, while its average price target of $251.52 implies shares will gain 78% in the year ahead. Adobe only receives a Hold consensus rating. Its $272.87 average target suggests shares have 12-month upside of 6%. (See ORCL stock forecast or ADBE stock forecast)

data.title: Dow Jones Slips as 10-Year Yield Climbs to 19-Year High
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is down 0.62% on Monday as rising Treasury yields continue to pressure equities. The 10-year yield is up 4.5 basis points to 5%, marking its highest level since 2007. Several factors have contributed to the higher yields, including elevated oil prices, stubborn inflation, and the risk of higher interest rates. Higher yields make bonds more attractive relative to equities and can influence some investors to rotate out of stocks.

In addition, higher yields reduce the present value of future earnings and also make borrowing money more expensive for companies and individuals.

Oil Surge Lifts Yields, Fuels Rate Hike Expectations

Oil prices have been a major driver for higher yields. Brent crude (BZ), the global oil benchmark, has risen 38% since the start of the U.S.-Iran war on February 28. That's boosted inflation expectations, pushing investors to demand higher yields to compensate for rising prices.

data.title: Wells Fargo Lowers S&P 500 Forecast to 7,700 as Political Risks and Tech Stock Pressure Cloud Growth Outlook
data.description:
Wells Fargo (WFC) lowered its year-end target for the S&P 500 index to 7,700 from 7,950 on September 14. Wells Fargo's research team noted that the stock market is entering the late innings of its growth cycle, a phase that often brings smaller price moves and lower valuation multiples. The updated target sits roughly 1% above the index's recent close of 7,619.98 points, placing Wells Fargo below Wall Street peers expecting the S&P 500 to top 8,000 by the end of 2026.

Even with the lower target, the benchmark index has gained 11.3% this year despite market volatility from Middle East tension and sticky inflation concerns. Second-quarter company earnings came in strong, with 85.7% of reporting S&P 500 firms beating Wall Street estimates. Looking ahead, Wells Fargo raised its 2027 company earnings-per-share target to $425 and its 2028 estimate to $460. However, analysts cautioned that 2028 earnings could drop if big tech firms slow down their spending on AI infrastructure.

Wells Fargo saw its own stock jump 3% after the release of their new stock market report.

data.title: Rocket Lab Stock (RKLB) Rises Today, Sept. 15 — Here's What's Driving It
data.description:
Rocket Lab USA (RKLB) stock is up 3% at Tuesday's market open after the company completed its At-The-Market (ATM) share sale to finance its pending acquisition of Iridium Communications (IRDM). The company raised about $1.944 billion in gross proceeds through the issuance of 29.3 million shares.

For context, Rocket Lab agreed in June to acquire Iridium in a cash-and-stock deal that valued the satellite operator at about $8 billion, or $54 per share.

Rocket Lab Clears Key Financing Steps

On Sept. 15, Iridium amended its $1.775 billion term loan agreement to allow Rocket Lab's planned acquisition to move forward. After the deal closes, Rocket Lab USA will provide an unsecured guarantee for Iridium's term loan. The company also terminated its $3.6 billion commitment for a senior secured bridge facility that it entered into on June 28, 2026, as part of the merger agreement.

Rocket Lab plans to use the net proceeds from its ATM share sale to fund the cash portion of its Iridium acquisition. If the deal does not close or the company has money left over, it will use the funds for future growth and general business needs.

The Iridium deal is expected to close in mid-2027.

Rocket Lab Eyes Bigger Space Ambitions after Iridium Deal

Speaking to World Space Business Week, Rocket Lab CFO Adam Spice said Iridium could help transform the company from a launch provider into a more complete space business. He said the deal would expand the company beyond rocket launches and spacecraft manufacturing into satellite network operations and services.

Spice further said, "When you double your company overnight, which will be the case when we combine the companies, you'll naturally have some dilution in that growth."  Rocket Lab has grown by nearly 100% a year in recent years, while the more mature Iridium has grown at a single-digit rate. This means the acquisition could slow Rocket Lab's overall growth rate in the near term.

Still, Rocket Lab sees new growth opportunities in Iridium's business. Spice said better access to capital and a stronger focus on growth could help the combined company expand faster. "We've got a lot of aggressive plans" to bring growth closer to what investors expect, he added.

data.title: Oracle Stock Forecast – Layoffs Mount as Analysts Remain Bullish
data.description:
Oracle (ORCL) stock remains under pressure as the company has reportedly begun another round of layoffs while continuing to invest billions of dollars in AI infrastructure. However, Wall Street analysts remain broadly bullish, betting that Oracle's rapidly growing AI cloud business can eventually justify its heavy spending.

The layoffs highlight Oracle's shift from a relatively people-intensive software business toward a more capital-intensive cloud and AI infrastructure model. In its latest annual report, Oracle cited AI adoption, strategic shifts, management and product changes, acquisitions, and efforts to improve operating efficiency among the factors behind workforce reductions.

Why Is Oracle Cutting Jobs?

In fiscal 2026, Oracle cut about 21,000 jobs, or 13% of its workforce, while spending $55.7 billion on capital expenditures, primarily to expand data centers. As of August 31, 2026, Oracle estimated that its 2026 restructuring plan could cost up to $2.1 billion. The company has also guided to roughly $70 billion in capital expenditures for the current fiscal year.

Promotion

200% short exposure to ORCL with ORCZ

The workforce reductions come as Oracle aggressively expands its data-center footprint to meet demand for AI computing. The strategy is expensive, raising concerns about leverage, cash flow, and whether the company can generate sufficient returns from its AI investments.

Analysts Remain Bullish on ORCL

Despite the layoffs, analysts see reasons for optimism. Following Oracle's latest results, Freedom Broker analyst Egor Tolmachev lowered his price target on ORCL to $205 from $210 but maintained a Buy rating.

Tolmachev said Oracle's latest quarter provided stronger evidence that its AI investments are starting to drive revenue, pointing to a better-than-expected backlog, infrastructure revenue that more than doubled from the prior year, and an improved funding position.

However, he also raised some concerns. New bookings and backlog growth fell sharply from the previous quarter, while the company raised its guidance by less than expected. He also noted that profit grew slower than revenue, partly due to a lower tax rate and higher non-operating income.

He argued that investors need more evidence that Oracle can turn its massive contracted backlog into sustainable revenue and cash flow. He expects the company's October Investor Day to provide a more meaningful test of its AI plans.

According to TipRanks, Oracle has a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 26 Buys and four Hold ratings. The average Oracle price target of $251.52 implies 73.7% upside potential from current levels. Year-to-date, ORCL shares have dropped 25%.
